subject: Commercial proposal and support pricing for Brightline
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@brightline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: 2026-05-01T17:12:00Z
Subject: Commercial inquiry: premium support for Brightline

Marissa —

Thanks for the intro last week. Brightline is finalizing our vendor shortlist and we need a clearer picture of Redwood's premium support packaging before we move to procurement. High-level asks below — can you confirm by EOD Tuesday?

1) Pricing model: retainer vs consumption. For a 12–24 month commitment, what does a hybrid structure look like (base retainer + consumption credits)?
2) Uptime and response commitments: sample SLAs for 99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99 and how credits are calculated (minutes vs percentage).
3) Escalation coverage: on-call windows, escalation path to engineering, and typical MTTR bands by tier.
4) Discounting: what concessions are available for a $1.2M ARR commit in year 1 and an optional prepay?

Attached is our RFP excerpt that lists expected peak QPS, data residency, and a rough incident policy we operate under (Brightline_RFP_Support.pdf). Happy to schedule a short call if it helps.

Thanks,
Sam Turner
Head of Infrastructure
Brightline

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@brightline.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Commercial inquiry: premium support for Brightline

Sam —

Appreciate the RFP excerpt. I sketched a concise commercial approach that balances predictability and flexibility; attaching a one-sheet and an XLS with the structures (RI_Support_Structures.xlsx). Key points up front:

- Hybrid model recommended: a modest base retainer to guarantee a named SLA and escalation roster + per-incident/consumption credits for burst usage. This preserves low latency for your burst windows while keeping unit economics aligned to usage.

- Suggested tiers (high level):
  * Foundation (base): 99.9% / Standard 8x5 support, 24-hour acknowledged escalation, 48-72h engineering engagement; best for non-critical workloads.
  * Business: 99.95% / 24x7 monitoring, 4-hour response for Sev1, 8-hour for Sev2; engineering on-call escalation with guaranteed callback within 1 hour.
  * Mission: 99.99% / 24x7 rapid response, 1-hour response for Sev1, dedicated on-call roster with prioritized runbook and a named TPM. Includes automatic fallback routing to regional capacity.

- Credit approach: calculate service credits as a function of total outage minutes weighted by impacted availability band (example: each minute below target maps to X token credits; credits offset future consumption invoice). We prefer credits applied to next invoice rather than refunds — simplifies accounting.

- Discounting levers: commit volume (ARR), prepay term, multi-year auto-renew, and limited onboarding professional services bundling. We typically layer a volume ladder (2–10% for first tranche, 5–15% for larger commits) plus up to 3% additional for full prepay.

Operational asks from your side to firm a quote: average sustained QPS during peak, typical session length, and acceptable MTTR target per Sev. If you can share those three numbers, we can return a firm price + a draft SOW for retainer scope.

I've looped in Karthik to provide a preliminary commercial sketch and Rachel on finance to check discount guardrails.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T18:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Commercial inquiry: premium support for Brightline

Marissa / Karthik —

Reviewing the sketch: for a $1.2M ARR anchor, finance can offer the following concession framework assuming a 12-month commitment with an option to extend to 24 months:

- Base retainer credit: 8% commercial credit applied to retainer line if Brightline prepays 6 months up front.
- Consumption discount ladder: 3% at $300k, 6% at $600k, 10% at $1.0M (applies to consumption tokens).
- Early-payment incentive: additional 2% off total invoice if full year prepaid via ACH within 15 days of DocuSign.
- One-time onboarding PS credit: waive first 40 hours of SRE onboarding for Enterprise / Mission tiers.

Constraints / notes: discounts are contingent on 60-day cancellation protection (no churn within first 60 days), and legal will insist on a standard SLA credit cap equal to 6 months of retainer fees (we should flag that to procurement).

I'll draft a short commercial term grid and attach to the SOW once Marissa confirms the tier selection.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@brightline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: 2026-05-04T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Commercial proposal and support pricing for Brightline

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and to Rachel for the pricing scaffolding. A few clarifying items before we lock in a call:

On the retainer vs consumption split — would Redwood model the base retainer to cover an agreed nominal monthly burst band (e.g., first N token-hours or baseline throughput)? If so, how do you reconcile overage during seasonal peaks?

On credits — Brightline prefers a minutes-based credit model that can be applied either as a service credit or as a reduction of future consumption fees. You mentioned invoice-credit by default; we're fine with that but need the formula in writing (sample calc for 15 minutes of degraded service at 99.95).

We'd like the draft SOW and a redlineable Term Sheet. Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute call next Tue (May 11) at 10:00 PT? If that works, we'll have procurement on the line.

On Tue, May 3, 2026, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> For a $1.2M anchor we can layer an 8% retainer credit for 6-month prepay + consumption ladder up to 10% at scale; legal will require a 60-day cancel guardrail and an SLA cap.

Appreciate it — attaching our RFP doc again for context. Please send a firm proposal and SOW ahead of the call so procurement can review.

Best,
Sam Turner
Head of Infrastructure
Brightline
